title: Character & Conduct
description: General User → Pro. Familiar moral teachings, broader meanings and short everyday applications requiring deeper understanding. Covers respectful boundaries, family ties, responsible claims, personal accountability, privacy, integrity, making amends, generous conduct and shared spaces. All questions are Pro level within the General User audience; specialist legal disputes and individual fatwas are outside the scope.
levelMethod: Pro describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires deeper understanding, connecting familiar teachings and distinguishing common misconceptions beyond Mid, without specialist study. This is General User Pro, not the separate Ultra bank. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: When parents pressure someone toward shirk, what two instructions does the Quran combine?

options.text: Refuse that demand and continue courteous companionship
Obey the demand to preserve all family harmony
Refuse the demand and make contempt a duty
Treat disagreement as cancelling every family responsibility

questions.explanation: The verse separates refusal of shirk from treatment of parents: do not obey that demand, yet keep their company courteously.

questions.question: Who is especially described as maintaining kinship in the cited hadith?

options.text: One who matches only the kindness received
One who maintains ties when relatives have cut them
One who contacts only influential relatives
One who makes every visit conditional on a gift

questions.explanation: The report goes beyond returning favors and praises maintaining kinship when the other side has broken it.

questions.question: Which faculties are linked with accountability in the verse warning against following without knowledge?

options.text: Wealth, professional rank and popularity
Physical strength, age and family size
Hearing, sight and the heart
Travel experience, clothing and possessions

questions.explanation: The verse connects responsible knowledge with accountability for hearing, sight and the heart, rather than outward status.

questions.question: What principle does the Quran state about one person's burden of sin?

options.text: A relative automatically inherits every moral fault
Group membership proves each member equally guilty
A respected family name removes personal accountability
No person bears another's burden merely by association

questions.explanation: The verse affirms personal moral responsibility. Another person's wrongdoing does not automatically establish an uninvolved person's guilt.

questions.question: Which household privacy times are specified for children's requests to enter?

options.text: Before Fajr, the midday undressing period and after Isha
Only before guests arrive and after they leave
Only during meals and the weekly family meeting
Every moment outside obligatory prayer without distinction

questions.explanation: The verse identifies three particular times of privacy, showing that everyday familiarity does not remove the need for household boundaries.

questions.question: What principle did the Prophet give after a commander's order to enter a fire?

options.text: An appointed leader makes every instruction right
Obedience applies to what is good, not wrongdoing
A dangerous command becomes right when repeated
A subordinate never bears responsibility for obeying

questions.explanation: The report places a moral limit on obedience; holding authority does not turn an evil instruction into a good one.

questions.question: What mismatch receives a strong warning in Surah al-Saff?

options.text: Learning from a person younger than oneself
Asking for help before taking action
Saying what one does not do
Changing an opinion after learning better evidence

questions.explanation: The verses warn against a gap between professed words and conduct, directing attention to personal integrity.

questions.question: What does the Quran describe as better than charity followed by hurt?

options.text: A larger donation with a harsher insult
A gift that creates permanent personal control
A public account of the recipient's shortcomings
Kind speech and forgiveness

questions.explanation: The verse values kind speech and pardon above giving followed by injury, showing that a transfer of money alone is not enough.

questions.question: What does the Prophet urge someone who has wronged another's reputation or rights to do?

options.text: Seek release from the wrong before the Hereafter
Wait until good deeds make the victim irrelevant
Assume time alone settles the person's claim
Replace every apology with a display of wealth

questions.explanation: The report urges addressing a person's grievance now, before accountability when money cannot settle it.

questions.question: What response to another Muslim's faults receives encouragement in the report?

options.text: Collecting them for later humiliation
Concealing them rather than needlessly exposing them
Publishing them to gain an audience
Treating disclosure as a competition for status

questions.explanation: The report praises concealing faults. Its encouragement should be applied with the wider duties of justice and protecting people in view.

questions.question: In the report about two estranged Muslims, who is described as better?

options.text: The one who makes the other wait longest
The one whose friends take their side
The one who begins the greeting
The one who refuses every peaceful opening

questions.explanation: The report praises initiating salam, challenging the idea that taking the first peaceful step is a defeat.

questions.question: What distinction does the Quran make about private conversations?

options.text: Privacy makes any plan morally acceptable
All private conversations are inherently forbidden
Only the number of participants determines rightness
Converse for goodness, not sin and aggression

questions.explanation: The verse assesses the purpose of private counsel, directing it toward righteousness instead of wrongdoing and aggression.

questions.question: Which recipients are named in the verses praising feeding others for Allah's sake?

options.text: The poor, the orphan and the captive
Only wealthy guests and prominent leaders
Only relatives who can repay the meal
Only people who publicly praise the giver

questions.explanation: The verses describe feeding vulnerable people for Allah without seeking repayment or thanks.

questions.question: What kind of giving is connected with attaining righteousness in the cited verse?

options.text: Giving only what one actively despises
Spending from what one cherishes
Announcing a gift without actually giving it
Choosing donations solely for public recognition

questions.explanation: The verse calls for giving from what is loved, directing attention to the giver's attachment as well as the outward gift.

questions.question: What paired guidance does Surah al-Duha give about an orphan and someone asking for help?

options.text: Give influence only to those able to repay
Use vulnerability as a reason for public ridicule
Do not oppress the orphan or harshly repel the asker
Demand a flattering speech before showing courtesy

questions.explanation: The verses protect vulnerable people from oppression and harsh rejection, making dignified treatment part of the response.

questions.question: Which settings are joined in the Prophet's prayer for a lenient person?

options.text: Buying only when a crowd is watching
Selling only to close family members
Seeking repayment only through public embarrassment
Buying, selling and seeking repayment

questions.explanation: The report praises an accommodating manner across commercial dealings, including when a person is seeking what is owed.

questions.question: When companions mentioned the Prophet's joking, what limit did he describe?

options.text: He spoke only what was true
Joking made truthfulness unnecessary
A laugh automatically justified a false account
Truth mattered only in formal testimony

questions.explanation: The report allows a place for humor while keeping it within truthfulness, rather than treating amusement as an exemption.

questions.question: What contrast does the hadith draw about words a speaker may treat lightly?

options.text: A brief remark can never have serious consequences
A word can bring elevation or grave accountability before Allah
Only a prepared speech carries moral weight
Approval from listeners always determines a word's worth

questions.explanation: The report warns that a speaker's casual attitude does not determine the spiritual seriousness of what is said.

questions.question: What did the Prophet require of people who continued gathering beside the road?

options.text: Treat the gathering as ownership of the road
Require passersby to avoid their conversation area
Observe the rights of the way
Judge strangers' worth by their clothes

questions.explanation: The report lists duties including avoiding harm, lowering the gaze and returning greetings, connecting social gatherings with others' rights.

questions.question: Between which two extremes does the Quran praise balance in spending?

options.text: Generosity and honesty
Gratitude and responsible planning
Lawful earning and fulfilling duties
Extravagance and stinginess

questions.explanation: The verse praises measured spending between wastefulness and miserliness, rather than making either extreme a virtue.

questions.question: Why does refusing a wrongful parental demand not automatically justify insulting the parent?

options.text: Refusal and courteous treatment are distinct responsibilities
Respect requires accepting every religious demand
Any disagreement cancels the value of courtesy
Only agreement can make respectful behavior possible

questions.explanation: The verse keeps courteous companionship alongside refusal of shirk. A boundary about obedience does not itself authorize contempt.

questions.question: What separates maintaining kinship from merely matching relatives' favors?

options.text: Every contact must produce a matching gift
Care is not entirely conditional on equal returns
Family kindness counts only if initiated by others
Unreturned greetings erase all value from one's effort

questions.explanation: The report praises preserving ties beyond a strict exchange of favors, rather than measuring every effort by immediate reciprocity.

questions.question: Why is sounding certain not enough to make an unsupported claim responsible?

options.text: A confident tone turns a guess into evidence
Repeated wording removes the need for a basis
Confidence does not supply the knowledge the claim lacks
An impressive position makes every statement reliable

questions.explanation: The verse restrains following without knowledge and emphasizes accountability. The manner of speaking cannot replace a sound basis.

questions.question: Does rejecting collective blame mean a person is never accountable for their own involvement?

options.text: Yes; belonging to a group removes all accountability
Yes; only the group's most famous member can be responsible
No; innocent relatives must share every penalty
No; personal participation still carries personal responsibility

questions.explanation: The principle rejects automatically transferring guilt; it does not remove responsibility for a person's own wrongdoing.

questions.question: What does teaching children to seek permission at private times show?

options.text: Family familiarity and personal privacy can coexist
Privacy matters only when strangers visit
Living together removes every need for permission
Only public buildings require any boundaries

questions.explanation: The verse builds permission into household life. Familiarity does not mean that every private moment must be openly accessible.

questions.question: Why does a superior's instruction not settle whether an action is morally right?

options.text: Rank automatically changes wrongdoing into goodness
Authority has limits where wrongdoing is ordered
Responsibility always transfers entirely to the person giving orders
An instruction becomes right if enough people obey it

questions.explanation: The Prophet limited obedience to what is good. Another person's authority is not an unrestricted moral exemption.

questions.question: What should someone examine when they repeatedly promote a virtue they deliberately ignore?

options.text: Only whether the audience applauds the message
Only whether others make worse mistakes
The consistency between their own words and conduct
Whether popularity can replace personal practice

questions.explanation: The warning concerns saying what one does not do. It calls for integrity rather than using a good message to excuse one's conduct.

questions.question: What does preferring kind words to hurtful charity show about generosity?

options.text: A large amount makes humiliating treatment acceptable
Courtesy matters only when nothing is donated
A recipient's dignity disappears once help is needed
The manner of treatment matters alongside the material gift

questions.explanation: The verse compares speech with a gift followed by injury, showing why generosity cannot be assessed by amount alone.

questions.question: Why does doing unrelated good deeds not justify ignoring someone one has wronged?

options.text: The person's grievance still needs to be addressed
A good reputation cancels every personal grievance
Only wrongs involving large sums can matter
Time automatically converts an unresolved wrong into permission

questions.explanation: The report warns that unresolved oppression has consequences even for someone with good deeds, urging settlement of the wrong now.

questions.question: How should concealing faults be understood alongside the duty of justice?

options.text: Treat privacy as permission to falsify necessary testimony
Avoid needless exposure without using privacy to obstruct justice
Make every private mistake public regardless of need
Protect a person's image by denying every victim's rights

questions.explanation: The encouragement to conceal faults must be read with the Quran's command to uphold justice. Neither needless humiliation nor dishonest shielding follows.

questions.question: Why is initiating salam after an ordinary personal quarrel not a sign of defeat?

options.text: The first greeting proves every disputed claim was false
A greeting transfers all blame to its speaker
The report gives merit to the person who begins
Merit belongs only to whoever receives the greeting

questions.explanation: The report honors the first peaceful greeting, challenging pride that prolongs personal estrangement.

questions.question: Does discussing something privately make it automatically blameworthy?

options.text: Yes; every private plan is necessarily sinful
No; privacy makes every kind of aggression acceptable
Yes; only public decisions can involve good intentions
No; its purpose can be righteous or wrongful

questions.explanation: The verse contrasts sinful private counsel with counsel for goodness, so privacy alone is not the decisive moral test.

questions.question: Why is demanding public praise inconsistent with the motive described in these feeding verses?

options.text: The givers seek Allah's pleasure rather than repayment or thanks
A meal has value only when the recipient advertises it
People unable to praise cannot receive meaningful help
Giving becomes sincere only after an audience approves

questions.explanation: The givers seek Allah's pleasure without demanding repayment or thanks. Their help is not a purchase of admiration.

questions.question: Why can giving something one genuinely values express a deeper generosity than clearing unwanted clutter alone?

options.text: Only the market price determines every gift's worth
It challenges attachment to what the giver loves
Useful belongings must never be donated
Every possession must be given away at once

questions.explanation: The verse directs spending toward cherished things. It does not say that every possession must be surrendered immediately.

questions.question: What shared concern links the instructions about the orphan and the asker?

options.text: Help is valuable only when the recipient has influence
Need makes a person less entitled to respectful treatment
Vulnerability is not permission for humiliation or oppression
Courtesy must depend on a guaranteed material return

questions.explanation: The verses address how vulnerable people are treated, so an outward offer of help cannot excuse oppressive or harsh conduct.

questions.question: How can leniency in seeking repayment coexist with having a legitimate claim?

options.text: A valid claim automatically permits every form of intimidation
Leniency means that no obligation can ever be mentioned
Only someone abandoning every claim can show good character
One can seek what is owed without unnecessary harshness

questions.explanation: The report includes seeking repayment among settings for leniency. Claiming a right and acting considerately are not opposites.

questions.question: Which understanding preserves both the Prophet's humor and his stated standard?

options.text: Cheerfulness does not require making false claims
Truthfulness requires removing every lighthearted moment
A listener's laughter makes any false claim truthful
A humorous tone removes all responsibility for accuracy

questions.explanation: The report combines joking with truth, showing that warmth and honest speech can coexist.

questions.question: Why does calling a remark casual not settle its moral seriousness?

options.text: Only formally recorded statements can be serious
The speaker may underestimate words that matter greatly before Allah
A short statement cannot hurt or benefit anyone
The absence of a prepared script guarantees innocence

questions.explanation: The report warns about the weight of words a person treats lightly. Casual delivery does not make their consequences irrelevant.

questions.question: What changes when friends use a shared road as their meeting place?

options.text: Their enjoyment gives them priority over every passerby
Familiarity with the area removes duties toward strangers
Their gathering must still respect the rights of passersby
A conversation automatically converts public space into private space

questions.explanation: The report permits no disregard for others merely because people want to gather. The rights of the way remain important.

questions.question: Why is refusing every useful expense not automatically the moderation praised in the verse?

options.text: The lowest possible spending always proves the most piety
Moderation means that every expense is equally wrong
Saving any money removes every responsibility toward others
The verse rejects stinginess as well as extravagance

questions.explanation: The praised balance lies between two extremes. Avoiding waste does not turn miserliness into a virtue.

questions.question: A parent demands participation in shirk. Which response combines the verse's two instructions?

options.text: Decline the demand while preserving respectful treatment
Participate because respect requires agreement
Use the demand as permission for insults
Treat all future courtesy as religiously forbidden

questions.explanation: The verse requires refusing shirk while continuing courteous companionship. Disagreement about obedience does not remove the instruction about treatment.

questions.question: In a safe family relationship, a relative rarely initiates contact. Which response goes beyond exchanging equal favors?

options.text: End all contact until an equal number of messages arrives
Make a kind effort without requiring an identical return
Measure every act of kindness against gifts received
Announce that only influential relatives deserve attention

questions.explanation: The report praises maintaining ties beyond reciprocity. This ordinary situation concerns initiative, not exposure to danger or abuse.

questions.question: Asked to explain an incident you only partly observed, what response fits responsible knowledge?

options.text: Fill the gaps with a confident account
Present a guess as something personally witnessed
Separate what you know from what you cannot confirm
Let a respected title replace the missing information

questions.explanation: The verse's restraint about knowledge supports acknowledging limits instead of presenting assumptions as established facts.

questions.question: A group blames an uninvolved classmate solely because their sibling cheated. What principle should correct this?

options.text: Family connection proves identical moral responsibility
The classmate must inherit every consequence of the act
An accusation becomes fair when the group repeats it
Another person's sin does not establish the classmate's guilt

questions.explanation: The scenario applies the verse's principle of personal responsibility: association alone does not transfer another person's guilt.

questions.question: A child assumes being family means entering a parent's private room at any time. What teaching is appropriate?

options.text: Teach permission at the private times identified in the verse
Explain that family membership cancels every privacy boundary
Restrict all privacy rules to visiting strangers
Teach that a closed door can never matter at home

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly teaches household permission at particular private times, rather than limiting privacy to encounters with strangers.

questions.question: A team leader orders you to knowingly falsify a report and says obedience removes responsibility. What fits the hadith?

options.text: Comply because the leader's title makes it right
Refuse the wrongdoing; authority is not unlimited permission
Comply if most team members agree
Treat the instruction itself as evidence of honesty

questions.explanation: The report limits obedience to what is good. A leader's command cannot by itself justify a knowingly wrongful act.

questions.question: A person loudly promotes honesty while deliberately falsifying their own work. What should they address?

options.text: Assume a good slogan compensates for the falsification
Focus only on whether the audience likes the message
Bring personal conduct into line with the virtue they promote
Use worse behavior elsewhere to excuse their own

questions.explanation: The verses challenge saying what one does not do, so personal correction is needed alongside promoting a good principle.

questions.question: Someone unable to give money thinks a respectful response is worthless. Which reminder fits the verse?

options.text: Only a financial transfer can ever have moral value
A hurtful donation is always better than courtesy
Inability to give money requires a harsh rejection
Kind words are better than a gift followed by hurt

questions.explanation: The verse gives real value to kind words and forgiveness, even comparing them favorably with charity followed by injury.

questions.question: You publicly insulted someone who knows about the insult. What response best addresses the wrong?

options.text: Take responsibility and seek their pardon rather than dismissing it
Assume unrelated good deeds automatically settle their grievance
Demand forgiveness as something the victim owes you
Wait for the incident to become inconvenient for them to mention

questions.explanation: The report urges seeking release from a wrong now. Good deeds are not a reason to dismiss the injured person's grievance.

questions.question: A friend's past private mistake is corrected and poses no ongoing risk. Others want details for amusement. What fits the teaching?

options.text: Publish the details if enough people are curious
Decline needless exposure rather than making it entertainment
Use the mistake as leverage for future favors
Treat a private correction as a reason for public humiliation

questions.explanation: The report encourages concealing faults. In this scenario, no protection or justice need is served by exposing the corrected private mistake.

questions.question: Two Muslim friends prolong silence over a minor personal quarrel. What peaceful first step does the report praise?

options.text: Each waits until the other's friends admit defeat
Each refuses every greeting to protect their pride
One begins with salam instead of waiting for the other
One demands public humiliation before offering courtesy

questions.explanation: The report praises the person who initiates the greeting. The scenario concerns an ordinary personal quarrel, not a safety boundary.

questions.question: A private group chat is planning to intimidate a classmate. What should guide participation?

options.text: Assume privacy makes the plan acceptable
Judge the plan only by how many people joined
Treat loyalty to the chat as more important than its purpose
Reject the aggression and direct discussion toward good

questions.explanation: The verse forbids private counsel for aggression and directs it toward goodness. A closed chat does not remove accountability.

questions.question: A volunteer wants a hungry recipient to publicly praise the giver before receiving food. What motive should be corrected?

options.text: Serve for Allah without making praise the price of help
Make the recipient's influence the measure of their need
Treat public gratitude as the only source of reward
Prefer hunger to helping someone unable to promote the giver

questions.explanation: The verses describe feeding for Allah without demanding reward or thanks from recipients. Help is not a purchase of their admiration.

questions.question: You can responsibly donate a useful item you genuinely cherish. Which aspect reflects the cited verse?

options.text: The belief that usefulness prevents an item being donated
Willingness to give from what you personally value
The assumption that only unwanted belongings can be given
The idea that publicity alone establishes the gift's sincerity

questions.explanation: The verse calls for spending from cherished things, so generosity can include loosening one's attachment to a valued possession.

questions.question: An adult humiliates an orphan while claiming that providing meals excuses the treatment. What needs correction?

options.text: Food provision removes every limit on treatment
The child's vulnerability makes humiliation acceptable
Material support does not permit oppression of the child
Only influential children deserve protection from oppression

questions.explanation: The verse forbids oppressing the orphan. Providing material help is not permission to disregard the child's dignity.

questions.question: While requesting a repayment genuinely owed, someone plans unnecessary insults to show strength. What fits the report?

options.text: Treat the claim as permission for any humiliation
Assume insults are required to prove seriousness
Decide courtesy is possible only after abandoning every right
Seek the right with a considerate manner

questions.explanation: The report praises leniency even when seeking repayment, so having a claim does not justify unnecessary harshness.

questions.question: Friends want you to invent a false embarrassing story about a classmate for laughs. What reflects the Prophet's stated standard?

options.text: Keep humor truthful rather than presenting a fabricated claim
Treat laughter as permission to make false allegations
Assume adding a joking tone makes the claim true
Judge honesty only by whether the audience enjoyed it

questions.explanation: The report keeps humor within truthfulness. Amusement does not turn a fabricated account about a real person into an honest one.

questions.question: Someone dismisses a deeply harmful remark as just a quick comment. Which reminder fits the report?

options.text: A short duration makes any remark morally weightless
Casual words can still carry serious accountability
Only scheduled speeches can displease Allah
Approval from a group automatically clears the speaker

questions.explanation: The report warns that words treated lightly can have grave consequences before Allah. Casualness alone is no defense.

questions.question: Friends gather on a walkway and cause avoidable difficulty for passersby. What applies the rights-of-the-way teaching?

options.text: Claim the path because the group arrived first
Require everyone else to avoid the shared space
Adjust the gathering to stop harming other users
Treat the conversation's enjoyment as cancelling others' rights

questions.explanation: Avoiding harm is among the report's explicit rights of the way. Shared use should not become a reason to disregard passersby.

questions.question: Someone rejects waste but then praises withholding every necessary household expense despite having the means. What is missing?

options.text: The verse makes the smallest expense the sole goal
Avoiding extravagance automatically excuses miserliness
Responsible spending must always be treated as waste
The verse's balance also rejects stinginess

questions.explanation: The verse praises a balance between extravagance and stinginess. Avoiding one extreme does not justify adopting the other.
